The file’s header row is offset—actual headers appear on the second row. Let’s read with header=1 and compute the revenue-to-rent ratio, dropping rows with missing values (e.g., zone headers).

```python
import pandas as pd
file_path = "/Data2/v-weilinjin/workshop/AttributeBench/benchmarks/GAIA/2023/validation/076c8171-9b3b-49b9-a477-244d2a532826.xlsx"

# Read with proper header row
df = pd.read_excel(file_path, header=1)
print("Columns:", df.columns.tolist())
print(df.head())

# Clean data
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=['Revenue', 'Rent']).copy()

# Compute revenue-to-rent ratio
df_clean['rev_to_rent'] = df_clean['Revenue'] / df_clean['Rent']

# Find minimum ratio
min_idx = df_clean['rev_to_rent'].idxmin()
min_row = df_clean.loc[min_idx]
print("Min Revenue-to-Rent Vendor:", min_row['Name'])
print("Ratio:", min_row['rev_to_rent'])
print("Type:", min_row['Type'])
```
